title: Tallyhook 4.2 Release Notes
key_sentences: It adds scheduled exports, replaces the legacy queue driver and drops support for PostgreSQL 12.
The old names are rejected at start-up with an explicit error message.
If the check reports an older server, upgrade PostgreSQL first and keep Tallyhook on 4.1 until that is done.
After the restart, open the status page and confirm that the queue driver is reported as redis-stream.
Scheduled exports cannot yet write to object storage.

rows: The value redis-list is no longer accepted.
Relative paths resolve against the data directory.
CSV exports dropped the last row when the file ended without a newline.
Timezone offsets were ignored in scheduled reports.
The login page showed the username in the browser title.
Webhook retries ignored the configured timeout.

list_items.text: Scheduled exports can now be defined per workspace.
Exports run in the background worker and never block the web process.
Failed runs are retried three times with exponential back-off.
The new queue driver uses Redis streams instead of lists, which removes the duplicate-delivery problem reported in 4.1.
The audit log now records the user agent of every API call.
1. Stop the web and worker processes.
2. Back up the database and the data directory.
2.1 Use pg_dump with the custom format so that tables can be restored one by one.
2.2 Copy the data directory to a separate disk.
3. Update the configuration file as shown below.
4. Run the migrations and start the services again.
Container image on any OCI runtime
API tokens without an expiry date

$ tallyhook doctor --check database
Checking database version ...... 15.4 (ok)
Checking pending migrations .... 3 pending
Checking free disk space ....... 41.2 GB (ok)

queue:
  driver: redis-stream
  url: redis://cache.internal:6379/2
exports:
  path: exports/
  schedule:
    - name: nightly-ledger
      cron: "30 2 * * *"
      format: csv
api:
  rate_limit:
    per_minute: 120
notes: Two-page software release notes in Segoe UI with two code blocks in Consolas (a shell session and a YAML file; indentation inside code is significant and kept). An inline code span "tallyhook.yml" is part of a body sentence. Section numbers are typed in the headings ("1", "2.1"). Highlights is a CSS-drawn bullet list (disc, nested circle). The upgrade procedure is a TYPED list: "1." to "4." at level 0 and "2.1", "2.2" at level 1, with hanging indent. The list ends at the foot of page 1 and the YAML block it refers to opens page 2. Table 1 has a rule under the header only and no other lines; its key columns are set in Consolas. Table 2 is a zebra table with a dark header. At the foot of page 2 two boxes stand SIDE BY SIDE ("Supported platforms" and "Deprecated in this release"), each with a level-3 heading and a CSS bullet list; reading order is box by box (left box completely, then right box). Running header (two parts) and footer (licence line and "Page N of 2") are furniture.
